 Bank of America survey points to later holiday shopping, tighter budgets
 By 
 Matthew McNulty - 
 11/02/2026 
 Facebook Twitter Linkedin Email Print 
 A NEW BANK OF AMERICA survey found that 29% of consumers plan to do most of their holiday shopping in early to mid-December, compared with 17% around Black Friday. Pictured is a sign advertising Black Friday specials at a Macy’s in Denver on Nov. 20, 2023. / AP FILE PHOTO/DAVID ZALUBOWSKI 
 PROVIDENCE – Black Friday may be losing ground as the centerpiece of the holiday shopping season, with more Americans planning to do most of their gift buying in early to mid-December, according to a new Bank of America Corp. survey released Oct. 29.
 Twenty-nine percent of consumers said they plan to do most of their holiday shopping in early to mid-December, up from 19% in 2025.

 Meanwhile, the share planning to concentrate their shopping around Black Friday fell to 17%, down from 25% last year, according to the bank’s 2026 Holiday Spending Survey of more than 2,000 U.S. adults.
 “Consumers are being more deliberate this year, from setting their own timelines to staying focused on their budgets,” said Mary Hines Droesch, Bank of America’s head of consumer and small-business products and analytics.
 - Advertisement - 
 Consumers are also keeping a closer eye on their budgets. Nearly half, or 48%, expect to spend about the same as last year, while 39% plan to spend less. Just 12% expect to spend more.
 The survey also found consumers pulling back from newer shopping tools. Seventy-two percent said they do not plan to use artificial intelligence tools for holiday shopping, up from 49% in 2025. Fourteen percent plan to buy gifts directly through social media, down from 35% last year.
 Online shopping remains popular, with 74% planning to shop online, while 54% expect to visit brick-and-mortar stores.
 Meanwhile, 37% of consumers have encountered at least one holiday shopping scam tactic in recent years, the survey also found, including phishing emails posing as retailers and fake shipping notifications.
